column3: All admissible w,A,V require a singular nonlinear boundary-value solution with two integral constraints; spherical profiles cover only a parameter locus. Isoperimetric constant and endpoint regularity need primary checking; no all-parameter route.
Typical continuous iid inputs and statistical-scale discrepancy require average-case complexity analysis; finite sign enumeration gives no polynomial-time algorithm or hardness threshold.
Uniform high-probability divergence of blocking number/q over projective planes needs correlated random-incidence estimates; a fixed-q certificate cannot prove the asymptotic statement.
Every d,s,n and the limiting extremal density are requested. Easy s=0,2^d or small d values are parameter instances, not the full extremal problem.
The all-n motivic integral requires orbifold measure and coefficient-ring conventions not defined in the record; smooth-curve local normal forms alone do not compute the discriminant-weighted series.

For every closed genus g>=2 the enhanced autoequivalence classification needs full Fukaya-category and scalar/shift conventions; geometric generators alone do not prove surjectivity or kernel control.
Actual Mordell-Weil rank over exactly Q must be unbounded. Selmer ranks, analytic ranks, large known curves and function-field families do not satisfy these quantifiers.

Large-data three-dimensional global Hall-MHD regularity requires exact system/dissipation and solution-space hypotheses; the record does not supply them. Axisymmetric or small-data results do not cover it.
Several complementary-prime-sequence growth and bounded-representation questions are bundled; density-zero complements alone solve only the quoted older premise, not these refinements.
Exact D(n) for every n plus attaining matrices includes unresolved all-order design existence. Brute-force finite optimization is not the requested explicit formula.
Every bounded operator on a separable infinite complex Hilbert space is quantified. Compact/normal/finite-dimensional arguments and Banach-space counterexamples do not settle this scope.

The word typical has no specified topology or measure, and the final attractor-dimension paraphrase differs from information dimension of mu. No counterexample to a precisely quantified source claim established.
All positive line bundles on every compact complex n-fold and every m>=n+1 require the sharp adjoint basepoint-freeness bound; curves or stronger positivity are instances.

All finite graphs require equality gamma=gamma_infinity iff gamma=theta. A finite fixed-point search could certify a counterexample, but known-theorem/counterexample bodies must be checked before such investment; no witness claimed.
The exact rectangular Zarankiewicz function and all fixed s,t asymptotics are bundled; K_2,2 constructions and generic probabilistic lower bounds do not settle this scope.

Strong and epsilon-weak Hall bounds are separate universal assertions; negative x is easy but positive x is the hard domain. x=0 and negative exponent convention need source clarification, not discovery credit.
One composite n with phi(n)|(n-1) would refute the statement; bounded search cannot prove the universal exclusion and no small structural counterexample mechanism is present.
Every divergent-reciprocal subset and every progression length are quantified. Positive-density or three-term theorems alone do not bridge the sparse arbitrary-length case.
Every odd integer >5 must have p+2q with p,q prime; finite prime sieving is only instance checking and no all-n constructive prime-pair route is present.

Classification and representation over both number fields and rings of integers are requested in all ranks. Field local-global classification does not by itself supply the integral representation algorithm.

The sharp 1/4 lower bound for every congruence subgroup requires excluding all exceptional cusp eigenvalues. The stated discrete-spectrum equivalence also needs care with residual spectrum; no new route.
Every integer must be four integral cubes, with signs allowed. Finite residue identities and searches cover subclasses, not all integers; no global identity established.
A prime strictly between consecutive squares for every n is required; bounded prime tables or intervals of larger exponent do not satisfy the exact scope.

The literal record gives no cardinality threshold or centroid-subset size and itself attributes a proof. This is a record review, not a complete quantified Kemnitz statement or independent proof-body clearance.
The literal prose attributes Hales's theorem but omits admissible partition/finite-perimeter and asymptotic conventions for the whole plane. No primary proof audit or fresh outcome claimed.
Chromatic-coefficient log-concavity is described without a coefficient normalization or explicit inequality. Known-resolution leads need actual bodies; no reliance on the open/status field.
The record names the subgroup-rank conjecture and public proofs but omits its inequality, reduced-rank and double-coset quantifiers. It cannot count as a complete mathematical statement review.
All stated ordinary E,p,L are quantified, but admissible p-adic Lie-extension/ramification conventions needed for the Iwasawa-module conjecture are not specified. No short finiteness mechanism.
The record explicitly says its exception/monotonicity formulation is truncated. Exact m_n inequalities and the treatment of n=5,6 must be restored before testing; no finite-sieve claim.
Uniform C independent of N is the crucial quantifier. Error norm, data v, solution u and MFS discretization conventions are missing; disk estimates alone do not extend to every analytic domain.

Every lattice, dimension and admissible volume require uniqueness, beyond minimum diameter. Symmetrization giving one optimizer does not force equality cases; centering convention must be checked before translation objections.

Every pyramidal-routing instance requires an optimal tree. Capacity y is not defined in the record, and the VPN/pyramidal tree literature is an immediate known-resolution lead; no new optimization route claimed.

True complexity depends on the ambient-group/characteristic and coefficient conventions. Arbitrary finite Abelian wording is broader than usual finite-field theorems; no domain-correction credit or exact universal bridge established.

Source Conjecture1.1 is repeated verbatim as successor Theorem1.7 and proved there from dominance comparison. Successor Section5 proof read; strict-comparison formulation has equality caveats, so no full dependency audit claimed. Exact weak endpoint is already public.
Literal ell and t(C) inequalities have escaped-newline corruption, and t=0 admits no smallest nondivisor k. Restore primary scope before any minimum-semidegree argument; no corrected-domain credit.

For every free word both phi=beta and the leading coefficient count are required. Type-B quotient graphs and characteristic are source-defined, and later word-measure theory is a strong prior lead; simulations cannot clear it.
All integrable connections and almost all reductions require the full differential-Galois Lie algebra from p-curvature. Nilpotent or rank-one cases cannot cover the universal statement.

All n>=2 and 0<t<s require a global likelihood optimum under the rank-two model. L(P), feasible parameter space and normalization conventions are absent; optimizing a guessed likelihood would not screen the source question.
All weights and standard/nonstandard levels require dimension sharpness and generation of all relations. Finite low-weight linear algebra cannot prove universal completeness of period relations.
Restricted linkage and all stated critical multiplicities require affine-category and periodic Kazhdan-Lusztig theory; a small rank table is not a full-scope certificate.
For every positive k and every minimizer, strict second derivative is required. The operator Q(alpha,1) is not defined in the record; numerical curvature estimates alone are not certificates.
A finite rational hyperplane arrangement controlling all unequal-parameter cells for each Coxeter group requires global structure; fixed finite groups/parameter chambers are instances.

All locally finite-dimensional trace monoids, coefficient functors and n require a derived-colimit comparison. Category/sink conventions and the a_i/e_i differential typo must be restored before a resolution comparison.

Primary Conjecture3.11 literally asks only for a sublattice representation. A finite distributive lattice embeds into a Boolean lattice via join-irreducible ideals; encode each bit by UDUD or UUDD in concatenated Dyck blocks. Meet/join are blockwise minimum/maximum. This classical adaptation has no discovery credit; no successor-clearance claim.

All surfaces, plus every irreducible maximizer outside N2,N3, are quantified. Excess is undefined in the record; Euler counts or one minimal triangulation cannot prove the universal extremal classification.

Primary Conjecture1.1 is the exact noncoordinate projection formula. Section10.4 supplies the topological proof from the measure theorem and variational principle; this is already a source-proved endpoint. Full CP-chain dependency audit not performed.

Broad generality and conditions similar to those in Theorem do not specify a process class. An iid large-deviation calculation cannot resolve the unspecified general statement; no full rate-function route claimed.

Every strictly decreasing finite sequence needs a graph realizing all surface crossing minima, separately orientable/nonorientable. Gadgets giving drawing upper bounds do not establish matching lower bounds on every genus.

All moduli and nonzero-determinant links require invariant dependence only on the least shared prime and monotonicity for every prime. The coprime case has no nontrivial coloring and needs conventions; small-prime examples give no full result.

Every n>=4 and every length 4..ceil(n/2) under delta>3n/4 must be forced. A monochromatic Hamilton or single-cycle theorem is insufficient; likely later dense-cycle results require body comparison before investment.
